I was checking out subverses when I saw a comment about Babylon 5 in the Star Trek subverse. I really enjoyed watching Babylon 5 a year ago when I bought all five seasons on DVD and started binge watching until I finished the entire series. It was amazing!! I can't really get into DS9 without thinking directly about Babylon 5. I am a huge fan of science fiction and this series really stood out to me. The characters, the story, the location... everything! I would like to know your opinions on the characters, who was your favorite and why?

My favorite character would be Dr. Franklin. I really thought his character had a great outlook on everything and he became a stronger person after trying to "find" himself walking around Babylon 5. To me, that was really cool to see a character go through a personal quest like that in the midst of everything going on. Then he goes on to say to Sheridan... "I realized that I always defined myself in terms of what I wasn't. I wasn't a good soldier like my father, I wasn't the job. I wasn't a good prospect for marriage or kids. Always what I wasn't. Never what I was. And when you do that, you miss the moments. And the moments are all we got. When I thought I was going to die, even after everything that's happened... I realized I didn't want to let go. I was willing to do it all over again. And this time I could appreciate the moments. I can't go back. But I can appreciate what I have right now and I can define myself by what I am... instead of what I'm not."

SHERIDAN- "And what are you?"

Then Franklin responds, "Alive. Everything else is negotiable."

That last line really made me think. Alive. That's how I look at everything now.
Who is your favorite Babylon 5 character?

Either G'Kar or Marcus.

G'Kar was just a guy doing what was right for his people, and Marcus seems like he came right out of the three musketeers, making for a weird swashbuckling in SPACE!.
Marcus is an awesome character with a rather lovely singing voice.
Marcus was definitely an oddball but his sacrifice at the end was unforgettable.
For sure, Micheal Garibaldi. "I try never to get involved in my own life. Too much trouble."
I always felt bad that Garibaldi started mistrusting everyone after he got mind-fucked by Bester and almost turned on Sheridan.

I always had a soft spot for Vir. He was an ordinary guy doing a tough job for a ridiculously demanding boss, which made him relatable. He ran a kind of underground railroad to help Narns escape the occupation, which made him a hero. And he also had the single greatest response to Morden's question, which makes him a badass. When Morden asks, "What do you want?", Vir responds:

"I'd like to live just long enough to be there when they cut off your head, and stick it on a pike as a warning to the next ten generations that some favors come with too high a price. I would look up at your lifeless eyes and wave, like this. Can you and your associates arrange that for me, Mr. Morden?"
That was one of my favorite scenes when they finally show Vir waving to Mr. Morden with his head sitting upon a pike. That was awesome.
